title: SLO Forecasting and Capacity Safeguard Guidance
author: Liam Chen
body:
Overview

This guidance defines how Redwood Inference forecasts SLO consumption, translates that forecast into proactive capacity safeguards, and integrates those safeguards into incident reviews, error-budget policy, and operational tooling. It is intended for SREs, platform engineers, and on-call owners responsible for model-serving fleets and the routing/orchestration layer.

Scope

- Services covered: runtime-api (text/generation), embedding-service, router-proxy, cache-service, and dedicated-gpu-pool-controller.
- Time horizons: short-term (0–72h), tactical (3–14 days), strategic (15–90 days).
- Not covered: billing/finance contract negotiations; those live in finance-and-legal.

Definitions and Key Concepts

- SLI (Service Level Indicator): measurable metric of user-visible behavior (e.g., p95 request latency, token error rate).
- SLO (Service Level Objective): target for an SLI (e.g., p95 latency <= 220ms).
- Error budget: allowed SLO violation budget over the SLO window (e.g., 0.5% over 30 days).
- Capacity safeguard: pre-configured mitigations (autoscale cushions, fallback model variants, regional failover) activated when forecast/consumption indicates risk to error budget.

Principles

1) Forecast early, act early: detect capacity pressure via both telemetry and predictive models.
2) Prefer graceful degradation: route to smaller models / cached responses before throttling.
3) Clear ownership: each safeguard has a single on-call owner and a secondary.
4) Auditability: all safeguard activations are logged and surfaced in post-incident reviews.

SLOs and Error Budgets (examples)

| Service | SLI | SLO (30d) | Error budget (30d) | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| runtime-api | p95 request latency (ms) | <= 220ms | 0.5% | runtime-sre-oncall |
| embedding-service | median request latency (ms) | <= 180ms | 1% | embeddings-team |
| router-proxy | successful payload ratio | >= 99.95% | 0.05% | infra-networking |
(Use these as templates; product teams must pin final SLOs during SLO reviews.)

Forecasting Methodology

Inputs
- Traffic telemetry: per-route RPS, token distribution, typical sequence length histograms (24h, 7d, 30d).
- Queue metrics: queue length, processing latency, backpressure events.
- Model-level cost: tokens-per-second per-GPU, memory footprint, kv-cache footprint.
- External signals: marketing promotions, platform releases, partner launch dates, known enterprise maintenance windows.

Process (automated + human-in-loop)
1. Nightly batch forecast: run the forecasting job that predicts per-route RPS and token load for short and tactical horizons. Command: 
   bash
   curl -sS -H 'Authorization: Bearer $FORECAST_API_KEY' https://internal-forecasting.redwood/api/v1/predict?horizon=72h > /tmp/forecast.json
2. Telemetry cross-check: production telemetry pipeline runs anomaly detection; if predicted delta > 15% vs. trailing 7-day median then flag.
3. Capacity translation: convert token forecast to needed GPU-minutes using the model performance table (Appendix A).
4. Runbook evaluation: if required capacity delta > 20%, surface to SRE triage channel and evaluate safeguards.

Capacity Safeguards and Activation Rules

Safeguard categories
- Autoscale cushion: pre-provision N% more nodes than baseline (default 30% for hosted tiers, 15% for dedicated).
- Model variant fallback: promote quantized/fast model variant for non-critical routes.
- Prefix caching promotion: temporarily increase cache TTL for repeated prompt patterns.
- Regional failover: shift low-priority traffic to a secondary region with spare capacity.
- Throttling & fairshare: apply global or route-level throttles with documented percent reductions.

Activation thresholds (examples)
- Short-term trigger (0–72h): forecasted RPS > baseline * 1.25 OR queue length > 500 for 5m -> enable autoscale cushion.
- Tactical trigger (3–14d): predicted GPU-minute shortfall > 20% -> open capacity ramp runbook and notify sales/CS for impacted customers.
- Emergency trigger: observed error budget burn rate > 2x expected over 1h AND p95 latency > SLO -> enable model fallback and throttle non-critical routes.

Safeguard Ownership Table

- Autoscale cushion: infra-scaling (primary), runtime-sre (secondary)
- Model fallback policy: runtime-models (primary), applied-ml (secondary)
- Cache promotion: cache-platform (primary)
- Regional failover: networking-oncall (primary), platform-sre (secondary)

Operational Tooling Integration

Telemetry and dashboards
- Dashboard canonical IDs: SLO.LIT.p95.runtime-api, FORECAST.shortterm.runtime-api, GPU.MINUTES.utilization.pool-1.
- Prometheus alerts (representative):
  - Alert: HighShortTermForecast
    Expr: increase(forecast_predicted_rps[15m]) > 0 and forecast_predicted_rps / rte_baseline_rps > 1.25
    For: 10m
    Labels: severity=warning, team=infra-scaling
  - Alert: RapidErrorBudgetBurn
    Expr: (rate(slo_violations_total[1h]) / rate(slo_windows_total[1h])) > 2 * expected_burn_rate
    For: 5m
    Labels: severity=critical, team=runtime-sre

CLI snippets
- Trigger autoscale cushion manually:
  rctl scale --pool dedicated-gpu-pool --buffer 30 --reason "preemptive cushion: forecast spike"
- Promote model fallback:
  rctl model promote --route "*.inference.lowpri" --variant qp8-fast --until 2026-02-12T06:00:00Z --actor $USER

Runbook: Capacity-Triggered Mitigation (short-term)

Goal: rapidly contain SLO burn and prevent cascading failures when short-term forecast or observed load exceeds safe limits.

Preconditions (check before acting)
1. Confirm the alert from the telemetry pipeline (link in alert context).
2. Verify forecast > baseline * 1.25 and current queue metrics are elevated.
3. Confirm no scheduled maintenance or platform deployments that explain load.

Steps (ordered)
1. Post an incident stub to the tracker with title: "Capacity mitigation: <service> elevated forecast/queue" and include forecast snapshot.
2. Activate autoscale cushion: rctl scale --pool <pool> --buffer 30 --reason "forecast-driven".
3. If p95 latency > SLO for > 10m, enable model fallback for low-priority routes (use rctl model promote).
4. Increase cache TTL for frequently repeated prefixes where safe: rctl cache promote --route <route> --ttl 600
5. If error budget burn rate continues > 2x expected after 30m, engage throttling for best-effort customers via router-proxy:
   a. Apply per-tenant rate-limits: routerctl set-rate --tenant <tenant-id> --rate 10rps
   b. Enable fairshare: routerctl fairshare enable --policy degraded-99
6. Notify stakeholders: PagerDuty channel #sre-capacity, Product Ops, Sales for impacted customers.
7. Document all actions in incident ticket and append telemetry snapshots.

Post-incident review and evidence collection

Required artifacts for incident review when a safeguard was activated (mandatory):
- Forecast snapshots (pre and post activation).
- Telemetry graphs: p50/p95/p99 latency, SLI violation counts, queue length, GPU utilization.
- Runbook timeline of actions with timestamps and actors.
- Decision log: why chosen safeguards were used and alternatives considered.
- Postmortem owner (must be an SRE not directly involved in the mitigation steps).

Incident Review Standards (tie to SLOs and capacity)

1. Include an SLO consumption analysis section: compute expected vs. actual burn rates and identify root cause of burn.
2. Validate forecasting model inputs and surface model drift if forecasts were inaccurate.
3. If a safeguard was activated, evaluate whether it preserved customer-facing experience vs. cost tradeoffs.
4. Publish remediation items and owners; prioritize capacity changes into the 14-day tactical backlog if > 20% capacity gap is identified.

Quality Metrics for Safeguards

Track these KPIs monthly:
- Mean time to safeguard activation (MTSA): target < 20 minutes from alert to action.
- Safeguard efficacy: percent reduction in SLO burn rate within 30 minutes of activation. Target >= 70%.
- False positive rate of forecast alerts: target < 8% (measured by postmortem-confirmed unnecessary activations).

Appendix A — Model Performance Table (example)

| Model | GPU type | tokens/sec | avg kv-cache MB | notes |
| gptx-base-8bit | A100-80GB | 1100 | 1200 | quantized fp8 path, fast for chat |
| gptx-quant-qp8 | A100-80GB | 1500 | 1100 | optimized for short prompts |
| embed-compact | V100-32GB | 900 | 200 | batch-friendly embedding model |

Appendix B — Example PromQL snippets

- p95 latency for runtime-api:
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service="runtime-api"}[5m])) by (le))
- SLO burn rate over 1h:
  sum(increase(slo_violation_count{service="runtime-api",slo="p95-latency-30d"}[1h])) / sum(increase(slo_window_count{service="runtime-api",slo="p95-latency-30d"}[1h]))

Appendix C — Decision Log Template (must be attached to incident ticket)

- Problem statement:
- Forecast vs observed:
- Options considered:
- Chosen action and rationale:

Change history and governance

- This document is reviewed quarterly by the SRE reliability council. Significant changes must be approved by the head of SRE.
- Small updates (labels, thresholds) may be made by the infra-scaling team with a one-week notification to reviewers.
